approval_source.question_set: The upgrade drill (simulation plan, T8): what RC2 is in CI, the notice in CI, and the first drill's scope

reason: The upgrade drill had a definition (launch-rehearsals.md, tools table) but no second release to hand over to in CI, no notice for CI, and no scope; mapping it also found that a production node could not start a later release (decided separately, P01_E05_LATER_RELEASE_START_2026-10-28).

decisions.question: Order of work
decisions.rule: The later release start (P01_E05_LATER_RELEASE_START_2026-10-28) comes before the drill, which proves it end to end.

decisions.question: What RC2 is in the CI staging network
decisions.rule: RC2 is the release set with only the application (consensus_stdio) recompiled from the same source, its own crate at another optimization level (build_release.py variant: cargo rustc ... -- -C opt-level=2, reusing the first build's work tree), so it alone differs; the root verifier and the migration registry stay identical. It is for rehearsals only, never a production release. What RC2 is for R04 on the real hosts is decided before R04.

decisions.question: The upgrade and handover notice in CI
decisions.rule: The CI timing profile's 20-block notice, approved for the kit replacement drill (P01_E05_KIT_REPLACEMENT_DRILL_2026-10-08), also applies to the upgrade drill in CI only. R01 to R06 keep the rehearsal profile's 720 blocks and R07 the production 120,960.

decisions.question: The first drill's scope
decisions.rule: RC1 to RC2 with the receipt-index migration (receipt-index-v1): the upgrade and handover admissions prepared, signed three of five with the rehearsal kits and admitted; RC2 staged on both hosts; the paired activation after the notice; RC1 stopping with exit class release; the switch on both hosts; a reconciliation before and after. A pre-activation cancel (L15), a late-switched sentry and a return handover follow later.

does_not_authorize: any handover, upgrade or run on a real host
RC2 or any variant as a production release
